snippet.title: What REALLY Happened During the Biafran Raid in Nigeria
snippet.description:
In May 1969, a pivotal event unfolded during the Nigerian Civil War when Biafran Commandos executed a daring raid on an oil field in Qua Iboe. This operation tragically resulted in the deaths of 11 Siem workers and Egyptian technicians. Amidst this chaos, three Europeans were captured unharmed, leading to further developments at the nearby Okai Field where 15 more expatriate personnel were taken hostage.

The captives included Italians, West Germans, and a Lebanese national accused of aiding Nigerian forces against Biafran troops. The incident underscored global dimensions of the conflict and heightened diplomatic tensions until their eventual pardon by Ojukwu after intervention from Pope Paul VI.
